business.body:
- Established in 1993, CARE Ratings Ltd (CareEdge Ratings) is described as "India's second-largest rating agency", licensed by SEBI and accredited by RBI, with "a credible track record of rating companies across diverse sectors and strong position across the segments".
- CareEdge Global IFSC Ltd is headquartered at GIFT City and described as "a full-service global credit rating agency, offering Global Scale Ratings, along with ESG and valuation services", accredited by IFSCA and RBI.
- CARE ESG Ratings Ltd is described as "SEBI-registered India's premier ESG Rating Provider (ERP)" and "Continued market leader position among Cat 1 ERPs with 58% market share for Cat 1 ERP, Issuer Pay's Model"; it is enlisted with ICMA for Third Party Review services and registered with the World Bank.
- CARE Ratings Nepal Ltd is licensed by SEBON and claims the "Highest market share in Nepal" with "Significant coverage of Nepal's financial services landscape".
- Group structure: CARE Ratings Ltd is the parent, with wholly-owned subsidiaries CARE Analytics & Advisory Private Ltd, CARE ESG Ratings Ltd and CareEdge Global IFSC Ltd, plus international entities CARE Ratings (Africa) Private Ltd (Mauritius), CARE Ratings South Africa (Pty) Ltd and CARE Ratings Nepal Ltd.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Strategic stake] The group-structure slide carries the footnote "*SBI and NSE announced to take ~10% stake each in CGIL" (CareEdge Global IFSC Limited).
- [Vision/Mission] Stated vision is "To be a global research and analytics company that enables risk mitigation and superior decision making"; mission is "To provide best-in-class tools, analyses, and insights, enabling customers to make informed decisions".
- [Demand driver — macro] CareEdge's own macro view frames rating volumes: it projects "India's GDP growth to be at 6.7% in FY27", and notes fund-raising was mixed in Q1 FY27 with commercial paper issuances up 18.5% y-o-y to Rs 5.4 trillion while corporate bond issuances fell 29.3% y-o-y to Rs 2.5 trillion, as "elevated yields on corporate bonds have likely incentivised large industries to prefer bank credit".
- [Bank-credit substitution risk] Bank credit growth accelerated to 18.6% y-o-y at end-June 2026 versus 9.5% a year earlier, with credit to large industries (67% share of industrial credit) up 16.6% from 2.0% — a funding shift away from the bond market that the deck itself links to lower bond issuance.
- [Management framing] Mehul Pandya, MD & Group CEO: "we reiterate that the Company's financial performance should be evaluated on an annual basis, rather than on a QoQ or sequential basis."

deepdive.thesis: The deck positions CARE Ratings as the parent of CareEdge, "a knowledge-based analytical group offering services in Credit Ratings, Analytics, Consulting and Sustainability", built around India's second-largest rating agency and extending into ESG ratings, AI-led analytics and a GIFT City-based global rating arm.
